message: StaffMemberDrawer.tsx now renders the Employment Type row via transformAssignmentCategoryGroup(assignmentCategoryGroup, t) instead of the hardcoded pendingField placeholder, but StaffMemberDrawer.test.tsx has no assertion on this row for either a populated or null assignmentCategoryGroup. A regression that reverts this line to pendingField would not be caught by any test.

MpdAssignmentCategoryGroupEnum is mapped to display labels in two places: the new transformAssignmentCategoryGroup helper and the filter panel MenuItem children. The repo rule is one enum value maps to one label, so the dropdown and the row/drawer can drift apart on the next copy change.

transformAssignmentCategoryGroup already returns early for null/undefined, so the trailing default branch is unreachable for every value the type allows. It converts a future schema enum member from a compile error into a silent em dash in the UI.
dismissalDetail: the default branch is a deliberate runtime fallback for server enum values the client doesn't know yet; the unreachable-branch defect is gone (the early null return was removed) and helpers.test.ts covers the unknown-value path

message: The test is named "omits assignmentCategoryGroup" but it asserts the variable is sent as an explicit null, so it does not actually prove the argument is omitted.

Test is named 'omits assignmentCategoryGroup until an employment type is chosen' but the assertion checks that the variable is sent with value null, not that the key is omitted from the operation — the name and the behavior it verifies do not match.
The JSDoc comment on transformAssignmentCategoryGroup only restates the function name/signature and adds no non-obvious why, which this repo has repeatedly asked reviewers to trim.

The repo keeps localized enum-label helpers as getLocalizedX in src/lib/functions; this one is named transformAssignmentCategoryGroup and lives in a feature helpers file. Harmless today because the enum is used only here, but it makes the helper hard to find if a second feature needs the same label.

pendingField is documented as "Stands in for fields managedStaff cannot supply yet", but it is now also the placeholder for a field the API does supply as null. Grepping pendingField no longer tells you which fields are still unimplemented.

The Monthly Gross Salary warning marker is rendered with focusable=false inside a CardActionArea that already has an explicit aria-label, so keyboard and screen-reader users tabbing through the report get no indication a staff member has this warning — only sighted mouse users who hover the red icon see it.

healthStatusLabel re-maps MpdHealthStatusEnum to the same four labels as the existing healthLabel in helpers.ts, differing only in case. That breaks the repo rule of one label per enum value: the two copies of the text can drift apart and add a second set of translation keys.

The legend hardcodes the fiscal-quarter month ranges as translated strings, although this same PR adds getQuarterMonthRange to helpers.ts to compute them. There are now two definitions of the fiscal calendar that can disagree.

The chip delete control is given role="button" and an aria-label but no tabIndex or onKeyDown, so assistive tech announces it as an actionable button that cannot actually be activated from the keyboard.

suppressErrors is applied to the whole ManagedStaff operation, but the report only renders staffError when the list is empty, so a failed load-more page (fetchMore, not caught) is now completely silent. It also skips reportGraphQLError in client.ts, so every non-FILTER_REQUIRED server error on this query stops reaching Rollbar/Datadog.

pageSize 100 assumes one page holds the whole result, but the API clamps `first` to 50 (MPDXSchema default_max_page_size 50; ManagedStaffQuery sets no max_page_size). For 51-100 staff, TeamSummary counts and spouse merging run over only the first 50 people until the user scrolls to trigger loadMore, so the summary cards show wrong per-team status counts.

grossSalaryWarning() and QuickGlance both evaluate only the primary staff member of a merged spouse row (member.quarterlyHealth, member.newStaffMonthlySalary come from the spread `...node`, never `partner`), so a merged partner whose own Monthly Gross Salary is below their own New Staff benchmark never triggers the warning or shows their own gross-salary figure.

t("{{count}} {{status}}", { count }) was added to translation.json as a bare key with no _one/_other suffixes, unlike every other count-driven key in this file. i18next will not find a pluralized form for this key, so the per-status count chip (e.g. "1 at risk") risks rendering the literal key or the wrong plural form, and yarn extract will re-split it into suffixed keys on the next run, silently dropping the flat key added here.

getLocalizedSecaStatus is a second SecaStatusEnum localizer; getLocalizedTaxStatus already exists and labels the same values differently ("Subject to SECA"/"Subject to FICA"/"Exempt" vs "Pays SECA"/"Pays FICA"/"Exempt from SECA"). HR staff now see two wordings for one enum value across HrTools.

The pendingField fallback branches in QuickGlance (empty departments array, null geographicLocation, null newStaffMonthlySalary) are new to this component and are never exercised: the only quick-glance test (StaffMember.test.tsx "shows the extra details when expanded") uses a fully-populated member fixture.

The team summary is derived from staffMembers, which is already filtered server-side by teamNames/search/department, so clicking a card collapses the strip to that team (plus partial counts for any other teams its members share). The cards cannot be used to switch team to team, and the "overview" changes with every unrelated filter.

useManagedStaffTeamsQuery() destructures only `data`, not `error`; a failed teams query silently returns teamCount = 0 and the whole Teams section disappears with no indication anything went wrong, even for a supervisor who genuinely has several teams.

QuickGlance.tsx calls t('Department') for the department label, but translation.json only has the pre-existing "Department: {{department}}" key, not a bare "Department" key — this diff omits the new key the mined i18n rule requires to be hand-added alongside its first t() call.

The summarizeTeams sort test only exercises the red- and yellow-count tiebreakers (Gamma/Beta/Alpha), never the final alphabetical tiebreak (`a.name.localeCompare(b.name)`) for two teams with equal red/yellow counts.

QuickGlance.tsx is a new non-trivial component (142 lines, formats currency/quarter/enum data) but has no colocated QuickGlance.test.tsx; its behavior is only exercised indirectly through StaffMember.test.tsx, so edge cases specific to QuickGlance (e.g. department de-duplication across partner teams, missing partner spouse fallback) have no direct unit coverage.

Unmerged-spouse name formatting (spouseFirstName + spouseLastName ?? lastName) is written twice, in QuickGlance.tsx:58 and StaffMember.tsx:104, while the other row-name rules live in helpers.ts (getRowName). A future change to spouse naming will have to find both copies.

Monthly Gross Salary below benchmark is flagged by coloring the value text `error.main` in addition to the existing GrossSalaryMarker icon+tooltip. The row view (StaffMember.tsx) only ever used the icon marker, never a red value, so this is a new, inconsistent way of signalling the same warning.
dismissalDetail: Matches the drawer, which already colours the value red beside the marker; UX retracted in debate

message: QuickGlance always renders a "Spouse" detail line when `partner` is set (merged row), duplicating the combined name already shown in the row header per the design spec ("Merged rows already carry both names"), but no test covers the merged-pair QuickGlance output to confirm or refute this.
The new error Alert has no retry action, so the only way to recover is a full page reload. The mined PR-history rule asks for an Alert with a retry affordance in place of the report.

The whole mocks object is now cast with `as ApolloErgonoMockMap`, so the typed GqlMockedProvider generic no longer checks the happy-path mockData in any test in this file. A misspelled or stale field in mockData would now compile and be silently ignored.

In supervisor view, a failed report leaves staffName undefined and dataLoading false, so AccountInfoBox renders an empty name line above the error Alert. It reads like a render bug next to the new error state.

The error branch is tested only as a dead end; no test covers recovery when the user picks another year from the header, which stays enabled in the error state. A change that latches the error (for example storing it in state) would leave the alert up forever and still pass.
The Try Again button has no disabled/loading guard, so a user can click it repeatedly while a refetch is in flight, firing overlapping requests.
dismissalDetail: loading never turns true during a refetch after an error, and Apollo already merges repeated clicks into the one request in flight

message: ExportCsvButton and the Print button stay enabled during reportError, letting the user export an empty CSV or print a blank report instead of being blocked like the sibling MPGA error-state PR did.
dismissalDetail: Export CSV and Print are not rendered when the query fails, since there is no data and so no transactions; returning to a loaded month is served from cache without a new request, so an error never appears next to old data

message: Both Salary Calculator useHcmQuery calls render HCM_UNAVAILABLE inline but do not pass suppressErrorCodes, so the global Apollo error link also toasts the raw API message ("HCM UserInfo report unavailable") on top of the alert, and again on every failed Try Again. This breaks the HrTools rule that a component rendering an error code itself must suppress that code.
dismissalDetail: kept the toast like #2108 so the HCM outage still reaches Datadog

message: The failed-retry test only asserts the button re-enables, which `.finally()` guarantees on its own, so deleting `.catch(() => {})` in handleRetry stays green while leaking an unhandled rejection. It also never checks that a second click calls refetch again, which is what the test name promises.
The new <Trans> string (Our records indicate... click "Request New MHA") has no matching entry in public/locales/en/translation.json, so the English catalog is missing the key.

isHcmApprovedOnly checks eligibility and approved amount on their own instead of per person, so an eligible user with no amount plus an ineligible spouse with an HCM amount shows the Board Approved card and hides the EligibilityStatusTable. The Salary Calculator already decides the same thing per person (useMhaRequestData: showUserFields = userEligible && userHasApprovedMha), so this is a second, looser rule for the same idea.

CurrentBoardApproved now has a hidden second mode (HCM-only) switched on by request === null, and the check is spread over about six spots (approved-on fallback, hidePrint, hideActions, two Last updated guards, two Approved on guards). A future caller that passes null for some other reason gets HCM dates and no actions without noticing.

The new per-person pairing is only tested on the spouse side; no test has an ineligible user with an HCM amount next to an eligible spouse with none. A change that pairs the user amount with eitherPersonEligible instead of userEligibleForMHA would still pass every test.

The positive anchor ("not applied" text from NoRequestsDisplay) does not depend on HCM data, so it can render before the Hcm query resolves and the negative assertion could pass before the user amount is ever seen. The local mutation check shows the two mocked queries settle together today, so this is a robustness gap, not a wrong test.
The removed t() strings have no remaining consumers but their keys stay in the English catalog. The repo rule says the orphaned key must be deleted in the same diff.

Only the ineligible-spouse half of the new HCM-only gating is tested; no test covers an ineligible user with an eligible, HCM-approved spouse. Mutating showUserRow to `true` or dropping `!userEligibleForMHA ||` from anyoneIneligible (MinisterHousingAllowance.tsx:133) leaves every test green.

After the first await findByText("Current Board Approved MHA"), the test awaits findByTestId("eligibility-status-table") even though the table renders in the same commit as the card (both gated on context already loaded), against the repo idiom of bare getBy* after the first findBy*.

usePdsSummaryData now requests constants for a goal's locked historical calculationsYear but never reads the hook's `unavailable` flag (returned when a year has no seeded constants), and no test exercises that branch. Before this PR the hook always requested the current year (effectively always available); locking to a goal's creation year makes 'no constants seeded for that year' a newly realistic path for older PDS goals with no test coverage or user-facing signal.

SetupStep.tsx and MonthlyReimbursableSection.tsx were changed to pass calculation?.calculationsYear into useGoalCalculatorConstants, but neither component's existing test file was updated to assert the GoalCalculatorConstants query is called with that year. Because the GqlMockedProvider mock for GoalCalculatorConstants is a static object (not variable-aware), a regression that silently drops or hardcodes the year argument in either file would not turn any test red.

The goal year is now passed by hand into three separate PDS calls to useGoalCalculatorConstants (SetupStep, MonthlyReimbursableSection, usePdsSummaryData). GoalCalculator does this differently: its context owns one year-scoped constants result and tells consumers not to call the hook themselves, so a future PDS consumer that calls the hook with no year will quietly get current-year rates.

The past-year comparison reads DateTime.local().year fresh on every render instead of capturing it once, unlike the repos established now = useMemo(() => DateTime.now(), []) pattern for long-lived pages. On a session left open across a year boundary the past-year banner/chip can appear or disappear mid-session even though nothing about the goal changed.

The new validator guard checks the sticky stableNonBackpayTotal (falls back to lastValidNonBackpayTotalRef), while useSalaryCalculations checks the live nonBackpayTotal, so the two exceedsCap answers split apart. An over-cap staffer who types a non-backpay amount and then clears it back to backpay-only sees "Optional Comments" and an enabled Submit, but Formik still fails additionalInfo as required.

`expect(calls.report).toBe(0)` can never fail: `calls.report` only increments inside `failCallsWhen`, and this test passes no `failReportCall`, so the counter is 0 even if the report query runs. The test does not prove the report query is skipped when HCM errors.

The non-array `graphQLErrors` guard is fixed only in the browser error link; the sibling SSR error link in src/lib/apollo/ssrClient.ts still calls `graphQLErrors.map(...)` behind a truthiness check, so a string or object `errors` throws inside the link the same way.

The new HCM failure path folds every Hcm error into the generic "Staff Expense report could not be loaded. Please try again later." alert, while the repo already has a dedicated convention for the Hcm query failing with HCM_UNAVAILABLE (isHcmUnavailableError + HcmUnavailableAlert). When HCM is overloaded, this page tells users something different from every other HCM-backed page.
dismissalDetail: it's no longer possible to get an HCM_UNAVAILABLE error on the Staff Expense Report except in an extreme edge case that isn't worth having special logic for

message: The reworded key "{{pending}} of {{total}} Pending" is not in public/locales/en/translation.json, and the diff has no catalog change.

The new sentence is missing the comma after the introductory phrase, and the trailing email has no ending punctuation, unlike the old copy that closed with a period. The bare address after a full sentence also reads as dangling rather than as part of the guidance.

The new no-restricted-syntax Trans selector is a fifth mechanically enforced i18n rule, but .claude/review/rules/standards.md still says "four rules ESLint enforces mechanically" and does not list the single-brace ban. Reviewers and agents reading that checklist will not know bare {expr} inside <Trans> is now a lint error.

The support link moved into a new SupportLink component, but LimitedAccess.test.tsx only checks the link by its name and never checks the mailto href. If the href broke during this refactor, all four cases would still pass.

Nothing in the jest suite can catch this bug class, because test i18n returns the key, so the English text looks right whether or not the key matches translation.json. The only guard is a complex esquery selector with no test, so a later edit could quietly turn it off and the bug would come back with every test still green.
dismissalDetail: lint rule covers it for now

message: The memoized schema local is named `EditAppealSchema` (PascalCase) while every other lane file uses a camelCase local like `taskSchema`. It reads like a component.
The yup test name is now t("Is positive?"), so it changes with the active language. No test checks that any of the 12 converted schemas uses the component t.
Yup test names no longer call t(), so the en keys "Is positive?" and "Is amount in valid currency format?" are orphaned. The repo rule says to delete orphaned keys with their last consumer.

The overlay only blocks the mouse, so keyboard users can still tab into the location autocomplete while the table is marked busy. Also, with cache-and-network and notifyOnNetworkStatusChange, hcmLoading turns true again on refetchHcm and dims the populated table.

The SECA note is now sourced from the hcmUser/hcmSpouse object (the separate Hcm query) while the dollar amount it annotates (calcs?.requestedSeca) comes from the independent SalaryCalculation query. If the two queries ever disagree on SECA status (stale draft calculation, HCM status corrected mid-session, in-flight refetch), the UI can render "has opted out of SECA" or "pays FICA instead of SECA" directly beside a non-zero SECA dollar figure.

The new "HCM has no SECA status on file ... the cap may be too low. Contact HR or Payroll to fix it" message is rendered as a plain <span className="explanation"> in theme.palette.text.secondary — visually identical to benign footnotes like the ASR backpay note on the same card. This tree already has an established pattern for HCM-data-missing warnings that affect a financial cap.
dismissalDetail: Author keeps the gray explanation style in this PR; the warning emphasis can be revisited in a follow-up PR if needed.

message: getSecaNote is a pure branching function (status + name + t -> string) but is unexported and only exercised indirectly through component render tests, not a direct unit test.

The shared hcmUserMock/hcmSpouseMock staffInfo blocks never set secaStatus, which was display-irrelevant before this PR but is now the sole driver of RequestSummaryCard's SECA note. Every other test that renders RequestSummaryCard through this shared wrapper now shows an unintended, unasserted SECA note.

getSecaNote re-lists SecaStatusEnum (Fica/Seca/Optout) in a second switch in this file, independently of src/components/HrTools/Shared/getLocalizedTaxStatus.tsx, which switches on the same three members. The two helpers legitimately diverge in output shape though: getLocalizedTaxStatus returns a compact chip label and returns undefined for a missing status; getSecaNote returns full name-interpolated sentences plus a 4th branch (an actionable HR/Payroll warning) that getLocalizedTaxStatus has no equivalent for. Revised per round-1 debate (UX, Testing): the duplication risk is real but narrow (if the enum grows, both switches need a new case), not a correctness or test-debt issue, since neither helper's sentence templates could be eliminated by delegation.
dismissalDetail: The chip label helper and the sentence note are kept as separate presentations on purpose; a shared label map for three strings is not worth the indirection here.

message: The "keeps going when a step throws" test only asserts localStorage was cleared, so it cannot catch a regression where a failing clearStore or caches.keys stops later steps. It also never covers a throwing clearDatadogUser or one rejected caches.delete.

The clear-then-sign-out sequence is now copied by hand into five call sites (logout page, ProfileMenu, ProfileMenuPanel, ConnectOrganization, Apollo error link). The next sign-out path someone adds can call next-auth signOut directly and skip clearing cached donor data, and nothing will catch it.
Redundant beforeEach mockClear in both impersonation accordion tests (Admin :266, Organization :130): jest.config.js already sets clearMocks: true.

shouldKeepOnSignOut is tested with hand-written cache names, and nothing ties them to the name Serwist builds from cacheId. If cacheId or the prefix drifts, precache is wiped on sign-out or runtime caches survive, and no test goes red.

`attempt` swallows every failure with no logging, so if Cache Storage or the Apollo store fails to clear on sign-out or impersonation start, the team never finds out. That is exactly the privacy guarantee this PR is meant to provide.

The IndexedDB connection is cached forever, so once it closes (the blocking handler closes it, or the browser drops it, as Safari does after backgrounding) every later clear() throws. Sign-out purge then fails and the signed-out user's cached data stays on disk until the next sign-in clears it.

Setting maxSize: false means the whole normalized cache (including HR, salary and MHA data) now stays on disk, where the old 1MB localStorage limit used to purge large caches. When a session ends by token expiry instead of signOutAndClear, nothing purges IndexedDB, so that data stays readable on a shared machine until the next sign-in.

Keeping the server HTML while CacheRestoreGate suspends depends on an unwritten rule: nothing above the Suspense boundary may change context during hydration. Only comments and React.memo enforce it, and no test covers it, even though it already broke twice in this PR (commits 393c6c928, a0e9c709c).
